paper.title: LM-Nav: Robotic Navigation with Large Pre-Trained Models of Language, Vision, and Action

patterns/main/observe_act_interface.md: - **Extra tools are optional and checked per backbone.** Tools are added beside primitives rather than replacing them, harness parse/coordinate/feedback correctness is verified before comparison, and effects are reported per model: optional hybrid tools raise the strongest model 82.3 -> 85.7 SR at 0.59x calls, while imposed waypoints lift weak models (5 -> 43 SR) and move strong ones by <=2 points (2607.26148#s2, 2608.03327#s1).

- **E01 (ablation, common_practice).** Hold the frontier backbone fixed and compare the proposed harness with at least one alternative harness or loop organization on the same episodes. For zero-shot VLN-CE the alternative is a rerun of a published zero-shot harness or workflow (2606.10577#s4, 2609.15195#s4) with the same model; for coding agents, a second deployable harness. — _applies when_ a claim that a harness (rather than the model) raises embodied or agentic success.

- **E02 (ablation, common_practice).** Attribute a gain to a harness component only through one-at-a-time toggles (leave-one-out or single add) with the backbone fixed. A cumulative stack (A, then +B, then +C) or a bundle-level comparison does not separate components or their interactions. — _applies when_ a claim that a specific harness component (depth tool, memory, verifier, skill library, plugin, feedback channel) causes the improvement.

- **E03 (ablation, common_practice).** Report the harness or tool effect under at least two backbones of different strength. Several read papers find that tools and imposed structure help weak models and are neutral or harmful for strong ones. A gain measured on the teacher therefore does not predict the gain for a compact student. — _applies when_ a claim that a harness component or tool helps in general, or that a teacher-measured tool value will carry to a student.

- **E05 (metric, common_practice).** Report cost alongside success: model calls, input and output tokens, wall-clock or per-call latency, and USD per episode or per solved task, including failed trials. Harnesses with similar pass rates can differ about 40x in tokens per solved task. — _applies when_ a claim that a harness, interface or distilled student is better or more practical than an alternative.

- **E06 (dataset, common_practice).** For a VLN-CE harness, report SR, SPL, OSR and NE on R2R-CE val_unseen, either on the shared 100-episode zero-shot subset or the full split. State which one, and do not mix subset results with full-split numbers of trained methods as if they were matched. — _applies when_ an empirical claim about a zero-shot or harness-based VLN-CE / ObjectNav agent.

- **E08 (reproducibility, common_practice).** State contamination and development-overlap caveats. Frontier 'zero-shot' describes how the model was used, not what it was trained on. Disclose whether the evaluation tasks were used during harness development, and whether ablations ran under a privileged action space that is not comparable to the benchmark protocol. — _applies when_ a benchmark claim by a frontier-model harness, or ablations run under non-standard execution.

- **E16 (metric, common_practice).** Break failures down by endpoint as well as SR: never reached vs reached but wrong stop (the OSR-SR gap), false completion declarations, stuck or no-progress runs, and per-task repeat patterns. Stopping is the dominant residual failure in the read navigation papers. — _applies when_ an embodied navigation or manipulation agent's success claim, especially one that adds a stop or completion check.

- **E20 (other, common_practice).** State the depth assumption behind depth-based perception tools (pixel depth queries, back-projection, stop checks): whether depth is metric and calibrated, and whether behaviour under non-metric or scene-dependent depth was tested. — _applies when_ a harness whose tools or gates convert depth readings into distances, targets or stop decisions.

- **E22 (reproducibility, common_practice).** Compare interfaces and harnesses at a matched interaction budget: the same caps on LLM calls, turns, wall-clock time and GPU. Disclose any asymmetry, such as uncapped turns or extra compute for tool runs, because budget endings drive many success differences. — _applies when_ a comparison between harnesses, interfaces or tool bundles with the model fixed.

research/reference/researchstudio-15-31/: - **Run an ablation that isolates the conditioning signal — comparing instruction, format, or retrieval conditioning against the same multitask training without it — to prove the gain comes from conditioning and not merely from broader exposure.** _(source: both)_

- **Provide a contamination or data-overlap analysis between the adaptation tasks and the held-out evaluation set before any genuine held-out or zero-shot generalization claim is accepted.** _(source: both)_

- **Compare against the obvious cheaper alternative — longer input context, nearest-neighbor lookup, or plain multitask fine-tuning — so the unique value of the conditioning or retrieval is established rather than assumed.** _(source: reject_reviews)_

- **Justify each component of a multi-module conditioning pipeline with ablations that isolate its contribution; shallow ablations over interacting components are treated as insufficient.** _(source: both)_
- **Demonstrate that the recipe is generic across multiple tasks or domains and explain how the conditioning signal is obtained without a manual, per-task search.** _(source: reject_reviews)_

- **Characterize sensitivity to the quality and coverage of the conditioning source — the demonstration or retrieval database — and to the distributional gap between that source and the test domain.** _(source: both)_
- **Report the cost of the added structure — token and API budget, number of model or solver calls, and solver latency — rather than only end-task accuracy.** _(source: both)_

- **Provide ablations that isolate each component's marginal contribution, and especially show the claimed load-bearing step is what drives the gains rather than extra data or compute.** _(source: both)_
- **Disclose the exact prompts and implementation details so the decomposed pipeline is reproducible and the results are not suspected prompt-engineering artifacts.** _(source: both)_
- **Demonstrate generalization beyond a single narrow benchmark or domain, ideally with cross-domain or real-world tasks rather than templates specific to one dataset.** _(source: both)_
- **Compare fairly against simpler unified or end-to-end baselines and against concurrent decomposition methods, clarifying precisely what is novel relative to them.** _(source: both)_

- **Justify that the decomposition targets a genuine structural bottleneck — ideally evidenced by an empirical diagnostic linking a sub-task to the final outcome — instead of imposing structure for its own sake.** _(source: both)_

evidence.quote: For all experiments, the weights of LLM , VLM , and VNM are frozen
evidence.support_explanation: No parameter finetuning is not no target-environment map collection.

evidence.quote: we first construct the graph by manually driving the robot and collecting image and GPS observations.
evidence.support_explanation: Target-site traversal constructs the harness map before evaluation.

evidence.quote: We tested our system on 20 queries
evidence.support_explanation: Twenty instruction experiments, not a large repeated-trial suite.

evidence.quote: LM-Nav can consistently follow the instructions in 85% of the experiments
evidence.support_explanation: Preserve the headline and its discrepancy with net-success table rows.
Net-success rows both0.8 versus narrative85%; planning0.9/0.8 averages85%. That reconciliation is plausible but not asserted as fact.
Joint reachability-aware search improves planning over landmark-likelihood-only selection.

evidence.quote: counts the average number of human interventions required per experiment, due to unsafe maneuvers
evidence.support_explanation: Disengagement is distinct from instruction completion.

evidence.quote: LM-Nav only focuses on the landmarks and disregards any verbs or other commands
evidence.support_explanation: Free-form command interpretation is narrower than arbitrary instruction following.
Frozen model outputs feed precise graph-objective optimization, not unconstrained direct motion commands.

evidence.quote: The LLM and VLM queries are pre-computed on a remote workstation
evidence.support_explanation: Offboard construction/query costs differ from onboard execution.

evidence.quote: We report the detection successful if any of the top 3 predictions adhere to the contents of the image.
evidence.support_explanation: The100-image/30-landmark metric is permissive, not a strict grounded path-success oracle.

evidence.quote: the overhead image and spatial localization of the landmarks is not available to the robot
evidence.support_explanation: Do not treat visualization-only overhead imagery as planner input.

evidence.quote: we report the average efficiency over successful experiments.
evidence.support_explanation: Efficiency is conditioned on success and cannot substitute for unconditional task success.

signatures.information: GPT-3 sees instruction/examples; CLIP scores landmarks against stored robot images; navigation distances, GPS and temporal links build a graph. Overhead imagery is not robot input.
signatures.operation: Extract ordered landmarks; optimize CLIP grounding minus route distance using dynamic programming/Dijkstra.
signatures.output: A landmark-respecting path of image nodes.
signatures.conditions: Landmarks present/recognizable; graph connectivity and distance estimates reflect traversability.
signatures.feedback: CLIP/navigation scores constrain construction, not execution-failure feedback to the LLM.
signatures.selection_rule/data: Graph objective trades landmark likelihood against travel distance and preserves order; likelihood-only control drops reachability.
signatures.persistence: Static harness design and per-episode context; no accepted cross-task optimizer change is claimed.
signatures.later_use: Fixed components are reused on tasks; within-episode context is read by subsequent planner calls. This is not measured retained self-improvement.
signatures.claimed_effect: Better valid/efficient route selection than independent landmark detection.
signatures.failure_boundary: Hard landmarks, lighting and ignored verbs can invalidate instructions.

signatures.object: Image path versus long physical traversal
signatures.information: Frozen ViNG-style goal-conditioned policy; front RGB,GPS,odometry/IMU; precomputed offboard route.
signatures.operation: Execute image subgoals onboard; compare against naive GPS-directed controller.
signatures.output: Jackal traversal up to800m with intervention and efficiency records.
signatures.conditions: Previously manually mapped target environment; outdoor Jackal-specific controller.
signatures.feedback: Visual feedback in low-level navigation; human safety disengagement.
signatures.selection_rule/data: Static solver path, not persistent accepted policy revision.
signatures.persistence: Static harness design and per-episode context; no accepted cross-task optimizer change is claimed.
signatures.later_use: Fixed components are reused on tasks; within-episode context is read by subsequent planner calls. This is not measured retained self-improvement.
signatures.claimed_effect: Follow landmark-defined routes over6km cumulative travel.
signatures.failure_boundary: No arbitrary instruction recovery, broad embodiment transfer or fully specified arrival tolerance.

gap.author_gap: Language-free self-supervised navigation policies cannot interpret free-form instructions; pretrained text/vision models cannot execute safe traversals.
gap.checked_gap: The explicit seam connects ordered language landmarks to traversability-aware paths; removing reachability reduces planning validity/efficiency, while GPS-only execution fails on obstacles.

lineage/closest_adjacent.method: Language usefulness plus robot affordance selection.

gap.stakes: Wrong routes or unsafe direct motions despite correct landmark recognition.

claims.text: LM-Nav composes large pretrained language, vision and navigation models without target-environment finetuning or language-labelled navigation data, allowing a mobile robot to follow free-form textual instructions over long distances in novel outdoor settings.

claims.selection_vs_test: Target-site graph built through manual RGB/GPS traversal before instruction evaluation; no parameter finetuning.
